chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “If a man says to his wife, ‘I did not find you a virgin,’ and he has no proof, the hadd is administered to him, and he is left together with her.”

So this does not contradict the first report, which said that there is no hadd upon him, because in the first report he only negated the hadd in its complete sense, while in the second report he affirmed it by way of taʿzīr, and there is no contradiction between them.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband says to his wife, without proof, that she was not a virgin?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal consequence of a husband accusing his wife of not being a virgin without producing evidence. It indicates that he is subject to punishment, while a later juristic clarification explains that the two reports are reconciled by understanding one as negating the full hadd penalty and the other as affirming disciplinary punishment by way of taʿzīr.
